text.p: Dutch supermarkets group Ahold NV, parent of the Stop & Shop supermarket chain, Thursday reported a 69 percent increase in first-quarter profits to 234.4 million guilders ($121 million).
It repeated its forecast that it expects 1997 earnings to be considerably higher than those of 1997.
Ahold said the sharp rise in net earnings was mainly attributable to last year's acquisition of Boston-based Stop & Shop.
The stronger dollar -- worth an average 1.87 guilders in the first quarter of 1997 compared with 1.65 guilders in the same period of 1996 -- also had a positive impact.
Exchange rate movements, mainly in the dollar-guilder rate, also contributed to the gain.

First-quarter sales rose 48 percent to 14.0 billion guilders ($7.2 billion). Ahold said the increase in first-quarter sales would have been only 17 percent if Stop & Shop had also been included in its consolidated sales figures for the first quarter of 1996.
